newsitem.title: GERMANY: European spring barley crops look average-broker.
newsitem.headline: European spring barley crops look average-broker.

text.p: Current forecasts for European spring barley qualities and volumes were average but the weather over the next six to eight weeks will be crucial for the final outcome, a specialist broker said.

Jochen Mautner (GmbH), who publishes a bi-monthly survey of spring barley crops with a view to suitability for malting purposes, said cold and dry conditions in February-April had left their mark on crops across Europe.

Danish, German and Spanish spring barley crops should show yield and quality losses while those in Britain, France, Ireland, Austria and Sweden reported better conditions. However, all also shared a risk of high protein levels because of delayed nitrogen absorbtion. Protein levels must be low for desirable malting qualities.
Sowings were generally completed on time and were up 2.8 percent on last year, said Mautner, whose November 1996 survey put the EU spring barley area at 6.05 million hectares.
Malting and malt markets were flat ahead of anticipated contract negotiations in the autumn, when EU producers usually explore domestic and third country markets, Mautner said.

Harvesting of spring barley will start in July/August in most countries, with Spain and France probably starting at the end of June and Scandinavia only starting in September. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
